newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares rally halted amid low trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares rally halted amid low trade.

text.p: After three days of robust trade, the Nigerian stock market paused on Thursday, with the all-share index ending at 8513.92 from Wednesday's 8518.61.
Dealers attributed the fall to an increasing shortage of funds, resulting in few movements in selected equities.
"Trading remained dull because there is no money to trade with," one said.
Nestle continued its ascent, closing at 48.90 naira, up 10 kobo. Texaco gained a similar amount to close at 51.60 naira.
United Bank for Africa (UAB) shot back into demand on Thursday, adding 120 kobo to 10.90 naira.
International Merchant Bank edged higher with a four kobo gain to 1.45 naira, while oil miller P.S. Mandrides rose five kobo to 6.00 naira.
Oil marketer Agip continued to slide, closing 30 kobo down at 19.00 naira.
First Bank lost three kobo at 13.43 naira and Afribank shed five kobo to end at 6.95 naira.
Union Dicon Salt, which announced a slight drop in its nine-month result, was unchanged at 51.20 naira.
